title: Q-CRIT-ACTIONS-BEATS: count scheduled GitHub workflows as beats in the Worker, so a workflow GitHub did not start is a missed slot
body:
**Owner:** operations
**Trigger:** LOOPPROOF-1 merged
**Done check:** grep:seed/worker/src/pulse.js::workflow:
**Status:** closed

code-task: repo=ultrastable/ultrastable path=seed/worker/src/pulse.js
code-anchor: export const LANE_LOOPS

cost-guard (which ran the repository-side criticality tick) failed on schedule on 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15 with the annotation 'The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased', and nothing noticed. The Worker holds a GitHub token: add a loop `actions-watch` that, once an hour, lists the newest run of every workflow with a schedule (interval read from its cron), writes one beat `workflow:<file>` per expected slot with status ok or error (not started, failed), and judge them in the pulse step with their own interval (loop_clock every_min). A job GitHub refused to start for billing is an identity-bound gate: one gate card, default in effect = the Worker lane (ZERO-MINUTES-1), never a missed-slot repair item per day.

size: M

**Closing probe:** grep:seed/worker/src/pulse.js::workflow:

**Disposition:** shelved (executor-failed, 2026-11-20T20:46:50Z, DISPOSE-1)

**Evidence:** the executor failed 3 consecutive runs on this item; last reason: _Stall: . Its closing probe still runs on every fleet pass and records `fixed` when it passes; the executor retries it when its open queue is empty (every 30 days at most).
